text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: P90 latency for generation API (hosted/us-west-2) crossed 3s threshold at 2026-03-15T10:02:24Z. Alert severity: high.

alex: ack. I'm oncall for infra. looking at metrics now — p50 is fine, p95/p99 spiking, GPU util at 98% on two clusters.

maya: I can join for mitigation. do we have a recent deploy?

sam: no deploys in last 30m per deploy-bot. logs look like sudden increase in large-context chat requests, lots of streaming sessions.

alex: hypothesis: streaming sessions are keeping kv-cache pinned and increasing memory pressure + long-tail loops. plan: temporarily suspend push/streamed responses for non-enterprise traffic in us-west-2 to free up runtime concurrency.

leah: agree. can we target by customer tier so paying customers keep streaming? we should avoid affecting enterprise SLAs.

eng-ops: we have a feature-flag gate and routing tag we can flip per region+tier. proposed command:

```
# turn off stream push for hosted, region us-west-2, tier: free/standard
rwctl feature-flag set streaming_push_enabled false --scope hosted --region us-west-2 --exclude-tier enterprise
```

alex: executing the flag now in canary (1 of 4 clusters) first, then monitor 2 minutes, then roll to remaining 3 if metrics trend down.

incident-bot: runbook note: "When disabling streaming, fallback behavior is chunked generation (non-stream) — expect median increase in tail latency for single-request churn but significant drop in concurrent resource usage."

maya: copy. I'm watching p95 and active session count. also enabling temporary rate-limiter on streaming endpoints to reduce new sessions:

```
# apply soft rate-limit on streaming endpoint for non-enterprise
rwctl ratelimit create streaming_global_nonent --region us-west-2 --limit 1500rpm --burst 200
```

sam: pushed the global soft cap. also bumped routing fallback to use the smaller-quantized model for long contexts to relieve GPU memory.

leah: outreach: support-bot, ping top 10 customers in the region with enterprise flag false and give eta 30m, mention that enterprise customers are unaffected.

support-bot: Draft for notice: "We're temporarily suspending real-time streamed responses in US-West to stabilize inference throughput. If you rely on streaming-based UX, you may see generation delivered as a single response chunk for up to ~30 minutes while we mitigate. Enterprise customers with dedicated capacity are unaffected. Contact support for priority assistance."

alex: can we get quick noise/impact estimate? which tenant IDs account for bulk of streams?

eng-ops: dumping top streamers now: top 5 tenants account for 48% of stream sessions. two are non-enterprise. recommending targeted quota reduction for those two instead of global flip if mitigation succeeds.

maya: can you throttle those two tenants by reducing concurrent sessions to 10 each? command:

```
rwctl quota set tenant-42 concurrency 10 --region us-west-2
rwctl quota set tenant-77 concurrency 10 --region us-west-2
```

sam: quotas applied. observing immediate drop in concurrent sessions from 3.2k to 1.6k overall. p95 trending down.

alex: roll canary -> full region toggle. executing full region feature-flag flip now.

incident-bot: lifecycle event: feature-flag streaming_push_enabled set to false in hosted/us-west-2 by alex at 2026-03-15T10:07:12Z.

maya: metrics: p95 reduced from 3.2s -> 1.1s within 45s, GPU util down to 64%. outstanding async queue reduced.

leah: customer impact: support reports 4 tickets so far from integrations expecting server-sent events; we've flagged them as "affected by mitigation" and offered workaround (polling).

support-bot: Notifying affected customers now with the draft message.

alex: next steps: 1) keep monitoring for 30m, 2) if stable, re-enable streaming behind conservative rate-limits and per-tenant quotas, 3) follow-up postmortem with root cause (likely long-lived streaming sessions + model memory growth).

sam: i'll capture logs and heatmaps for the 30m window and prepare a quick dashboard (p50/p95/p99, gpu util, active streams, queue length).

maya: oncall handoff in 20m. alex, do you want to handoff to me once stability confirmed?

alex: yes — i'll document the state in ops-runbook and handoff to maya at :hand: 10:27Z.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: incident acknowledged and mitigation in place. Incident status: mitigated (live measures).

leah: noted for postmortem: consider autoscaling policy tweak for streaming-heavy traffic and TTL on long-lived KV caches.

alex: thanks team. I'll follow-up with timeline for re-enable and a short postmortem draft.

maya: i'll take next oncall rotation. staying on watch. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
